content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Using AWR and ADDM Reports in Oracle DB"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Automatic Workload Repository (AWR) and Automatic Database Diagnostic Monitor (ADDM) are powerful tools in Oracle Database for performance monitoring and tuning. AWR collects database statistics, and ADDM analyzes this data to identify performance bottlenecks and provide recommendations."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Generating AWR Reports"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"AWR reports can be generated using SQL*Plus or Oracle Enterprise Manager (OEM). Here's how to generate them using SQL*Plus:"},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"SQL> @$ORACLE_HOME/rdbms/admin/awrrpt.sql"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"The script will prompt you for the following information:"},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Report type: HTML or TEXT"},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Number of days of snapshots to choose from"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Beginning Snapshot ID"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ending Snapshot ID"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"After providing the required information, the AWR report will be generated in the specified format. The report file will be located in the directory from which you executed the script."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Generating ADDM Reports"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"ADDM reports are typically generated automatically after each AWR snapshot. However, you can also generate them manually using SQL*Plus:"},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"SQL> @$ORACLE_HOME/rdbms/admin/addmrpt.sql"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"The script will prompt you for the following information:"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Report type: HTML or TEXT"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Database ID"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Instance Number"},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Beginning Snapshot ID"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ending Snapshot ID"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"After providing the required information, the ADDM report will be generated in the specified format. The report file will be located in the directory from which you executed the script."},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Analyzing AWR Reports"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"AWR reports provide a wealth of information about database performance. Key sections to analyze include:"},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Load Profile: Shows the overall database load, including CPU usage, I/O, and network traffic."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Instance Efficiency Percentages: Indicates the efficiency of various database operations."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Top 5 Timed Events: Identifies the events that consume the most database time."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Wait Events: Provides detailed information about wait events, including the time spent waiting and the objects being waited on."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"SQL Statistics: Shows the SQL statements that consume the most resources, including CPU time, I/O, and execution count."},{"order":29,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Operating System Statistics: Provides information about the operating system's resource usage."},{"order":30,"type":"subheading","text":"Analyzing ADDM Reports"},{"order":31,"type":"paragraph","text":"ADDM reports provide a high-level overview of database performance issues and recommendations for resolving them. The report identifies performance bottlenecks and provides actionable advice."},{"order":32,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Findings: Describes the performance issues identified by ADDM."},{"order":33,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Recommendations: Provides suggestions for resolving the identified performance issues. These recommendations may include creating indexes, tuning SQL statements, or adjusting database parameters."},{"order":34,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Rationale: Explains the reasoning behind the recommendations."},{"order":35,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Impact: Estimates the potential impact of implementing the recommendations."},{"order":36,"type":"subheading","text":"Example Scenario"},{"order":37,"type":"paragraph","text":"Suppose an AWR report shows that the \"db file sequential read\" wait event is consuming a significant amount of database time. An ADDM report might identify a specific SQL statement that is performing poorly due to a missing index. The ADDM report would recommend creating an index on the appropriate column(s) to improve the performance of the SQL statement and reduce the \"db file sequential read\" wait time."},{"order":38,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices"},{"order":39,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Generate AWR reports regularly (e.g., daily or weekly) to monitor database performance trends."},{"order":40,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Review ADDM reports after each AWR snapshot to identify and address performance issues proactively."},{"order":41,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use AWR and ADDM reports in conjunction with other performance monitoring tools to gain a comprehensive understanding of database performance."},{"order":42,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Consider using Oracle Enterprise Manager (OEM) for a graphical interface to generate and analyze AWR and ADDM reports."},{"order":43,"type":"paragraph","text":"By effectively using AWR and ADDM reports, you can identify and resolve performance bottlenecks, optimize database performance, and ensure the smooth operation of your Oracle database."}]
